name: Elioenai
title: Descendant of David in the Time of Return
summary: Elioenai (also spelled Elioenaj) was a descendant of King David through the line of Zerubbabel, mentioned in the Books of Chronicles. He belonged to the royal lineage during the period after the exile in Babylon and represents the continuity of David's line following the return to Judah. The name means 'my eyes are turned toward the Lord'.

keyEvents.title: Elhoenai's Place in David's Lineage
keyEvents.description: Elhoenai is mentioned as the son of Neariah in the royal lineage after David, which continued after the Babylonian exile.

keyEvents.title: Elhoenai's Seven Sons
keyEvents.description: Elhoenai had seven sons, showing that David's royal lineage continued to grow after the return from Babylon.

keyEvents.title: David's Lineage Preserved Through the Exile
keyEvents.description: The genealogies in Chronicles show how David's line was preserved through generations from Zerubbabel up to Elhoenai, as a sign of God's faithfulness to His promises.

keyEvents.title: Another Elhoenai Among Those Who Married Foreign Women
keyEvents.description: A man named Elhoenai, son of Seraiah, is mentioned among the priests who had taken foreign wives and committed to sending them away during Ezra's reforms.

keyEvents.title: Elhoenai as a Temple Gatekeeper
keyEvents.description: An Elhoenai is also mentioned as a gatekeeper or guardian at the temple in connection with service in God's house after the return.
